lesson.title: Niet & Geen
lesson.subtitle: niet for the sentence, geen for an indefinite noun

hook.title: Two Negators, One Decision
hook.content: Dutch splits negation in two. Niet negates a verb, an adjective, a definite noun or a whole predicate; geen negates an indefinite noun. The choice is grammatical, not stylistic.

pattern.title: Ask what you are negating
pattern.content: Ik werk niet: niet negates the verb. Ik heb geen tijd: tijd is indefinite, so geen. Ik heb de tijd niet: the definite article pulls the sentence back to niet. The noun's definiteness decides.
pattern.linguist_note: Geen is a negative indefinite article; niet is the general negator. English uses 'not' and 'no' in a similar division, but Dutch makes the choice more systematically.
pattern.trap_note: Do not say ik heb niet tijd. Tijd has no article here, so it is indefinite and takes geen.

exercises.prompt: Match each English meaning with its Dutch twin (Niet & Geen):
exercises.target_answer: niet, geen, de tijd, het geld, werken, hebben
exercises.meaning: not, no, none, time, money, to work, to have
exercises.explanation: These are the anchors of "Niet & Geen": read each Dutch form through the pattern, not as a new word.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence says: “I do not work.”?
exercises.explanation: “Ik werk niet.” is the Dutch form; the other readings bend the pattern of “Niet & Geen”.

cues: The pattern: Ask what you are negating
It means: I have no time.
exercises.explanation: “Ik heb geen tijd.” puts the thought together the Dutch way — Ask what you are negating.

diagnosis.slip: an English-shaped word order slipped in
diagnosis.cue: Do not say ik heb niet tijd. Tijd has no article here, so it is indefinite and takes geen.

exercises.prompt: Which English sentence is built the Dutch way?
exercises.explanation: “Wij hebben geen geld.” is word-for-word “We have no money.”. The odd English is the lesson — never a model to produce. Pattern: Ask what you are negating.

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
cues: It means: He is not here.
exercises.explanation: “Hij is niet hier.” reuses only material taught in “Niet & Geen” — Ask what you are negating.
exercises.affirmation: You heard “Hij is niet hier.” — a sentence built from the lesson's own Dutch, practising Ask what you are negating.

twist.prompt: One more, no safety net — say: “I am not hungry.”
twist.explanation: Honger is an indefinite noun, so the negator is geen, not niet.

summary.outcome: Choose niet or geen by what follows and place it in the Dutch sentence.
summary.takeaway: Negation is a decision about the noun phrase, not a single word you sprinkle on a sentence.
summary.curiosity_teaser: Up next on De Brug: Niet/Geen Drill.

niet.etymology_derivation: The general negator; geen is its partner before indefinite nouns.

geen.etymology_derivation: The negative indefinite article: ne + een, the twin of English no.

tijd.etymology_derivation: English tide and Dutch tijd are the same word; English narrowed it to the sea.

geld.etymology_derivation: English geld is archaic; Dutch geld is everyday money.

werken.etymology_derivation: English work and Dutch werken are the same verb.

hebben.etymology_derivation: English have and Dutch hebben descend from the same verb; the b is preserved.
